items.text:
• 𝗠𝗼𝗹𝗲𝗰𝘂𝗹𝗮𝗿 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴 & 𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗳𝘁 𝗶𝗻𝗷𝘂𝗿𝘆
Toth et al. - Association of eplet mismatch load and allograft injury in kidney transplant recipients. Clinical Kidney Journal, 2026;19:sfag341.
Online: 26 Sep 2026.

In 657 kidney recipients, higher class II eplet load was associated with first-year injury, but discrimination did not exceed antigen matching. Single-centre retrospective data, mixed typing resolution and internally derived thresholds limit generalisability.

https://doi.org/10.1093/ckj/sfag341

evidence.finding: In 657 kidney recipients, higher class II eplet load was associated with first-year injury, but discrimination did not exceed antigen matching.
evidence.limitation: Single-centre retrospective data, mixed typing resolution and internally derived thresholds limit generalisability.
evidence.selectionReason: Direct head-to-head benchmark and integration of DSA, biopsy, MMDx and dd-cfDNA separate association from incremental predictive utility.

sources.label: Publisher main text: first-online history; Methods (typing, outcomes, statistics); Results, Tables 3-4 and Figures 5-7 captions; Discussion limitations. Supplement not reviewed.

items.text:
• 𝗡𝗞 𝗲𝗱𝘂𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 & 𝗛𝗦𝗖𝗧 𝗲𝗻𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗳𝘁𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁
Ding et al. - Donor-derived unlicensed NK cells promote hematopoietic engraftment and survival after allogeneic HSCT. Science Bulletin, 2026.
Online: 11 Oct 2026.

In 976 haploidentical HSCT recipients, donor unlicensed NK status was associated with faster recovery and better survival; experiments supported a role in progenitor expansion. Propensity matching does not establish clinical benefit from selecting donors or infusing these cells.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scib.2026.10.003

evidence.finding: In 976 haploidentical HSCT recipients, donor unlicensed NK status was associated with faster recovery and better survival; experiments supported a role in progenitor expansion.
evidence.limitation: Propensity matching does not establish clinical benefit from selecting donors or infusing these cells.
evidence.selectionReason: Large clinical cohort plus experimental work links NK education to engraftment, beyond graft-versus-leukaemia associations.

sources.label: Publisher indexed abstract and PubMed record PMID 42919759 reviewed; direct full text returned 403. First-online date verified in PubMed article-date metadata; publisher date could not be independently read.
Primary bibliographic record; article date, author list, journal-article status and abstract.

items.text:
• 𝗧𝗖𝗥 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗴𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 & 𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗶𝗺𝗺𝘂𝗻𝗼𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗲𝘁𝗶𝗰𝘀
Akıl et al. - Unveiling structural determinants of peptide recognition by public and private SARS-CoV-2-specific T-cell receptors. Nature Communications, 2026;17:11026.
Online: 22 Sep 2026.

Two TCRs with near-identical beta chains but different alpha chains used distinct peptide-HLA contacts despite similar affinity. Cryo-EM and mutagenesis expose limits of beta-chain-only inference; the study addresses one viral epitope, not alloreactivity.

https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-77827-z

evidence.finding: Two TCRs with near-identical beta chains but different alpha chains used distinct peptide-HLA contacts despite similar affinity.
evidence.limitation: Cryo-EM and mutagenesis expose limits of beta-chain-only inference; the study addresses one viral epitope, not alloreactivity.
evidence.selectionReason: Paired-chain structural evidence challenges beta-chain-based specificity assumptions relevant across infection, cancer and alloimmune repertoire research; nearing window expiry.

sources.label: Publisher indexed abstract and publication history; PubMed PMID 42907447. Full HTML/PDF access failed at Nature identity redirect. No figure-level or supplement audit claimed.

items.text:
From our Journal HLA Immune Response Genetics:
• 𝗔𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆 𝗲𝗽𝗶𝘁𝗼𝗽𝗲𝘀 & 𝗮𝘀𝘀𝗮𝘆 𝗱𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻
Meng et al. - AminoAcid3D: designing HLA single antigen panels and predicting essential epitope regions from antibody reactivity. HLA, 2026;108:e71049.
Online: 21 Oct 2026.

AA3D combines HLA sequence, structure and SAB reactivity to nominate candidate antibody-contact residues with variable patch size. These are epitope hypotheses, not verified binding sites or clinical specificity; independent validation remains to be assessed.

https://doi.org/10.1111/tan.71049

evidence.finding: AA3D combines HLA sequence, structure and SAB reactivity to nominate candidate antibody-contact residues with variable patch size.
evidence.limitation: These are epitope hypotheses, not verified binding sites or clinical specificity; independent validation remains to be assessed.
evidence.selectionReason: Substantive house-journal methods contribution relevant to antibody specificity and SAB-panel coverage; manufacturer-authored work, independent benchmarking not audited.

sources.label: Publisher abstract, original-article status, authors/affiliations and first-online date read via publisher abstract page; PubMed PMID 42908172. Full request redirected to abstract.

• 𝗡𝗞 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗲𝗽𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀 & 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺 𝗰𝗲𝗹𝗹 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻
Gottschalk et al. - Novel KIR2DS4:HLA-B*35 interaction predicts HLA-B*35 positive patient survival post hematopoietic stem cell transplant. Blood Advances, 2026.
Online: 30 Sep 2026.

Cell avidity and cytotoxicity assays supported a KIR2DS4 interaction with HLA-B*35. Donor KIR2DS4 genotype was associated with survival in an NK cell addback cohort and an independent matched HCT cohort. These observational comparisons do not establish benefit from genotype-guided donor selection.

https://doi.org/10.1182/bloodadvances.2026020173

evidence.finding: Cell avidity and cytotoxicity assays supported a KIR2DS4 interaction with HLA-B*35. Donor KIR2DS4 genotype was associated with survival in an NK cell addback cohort and an independent matched HCT cohort.
evidence.limitation: These observational comparisons do not establish benefit from genotype-guided donor selection.
evidence.selectionReason: Functional evidence for a KIR-HLA interaction paired with an independent clinical cohort.

sources.label: Publisher-supplied abstract and online-first metadata; ASH full text inaccessible.

items.text:
• 𝗦𝗼𝗹𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗛𝗟𝗔 & 𝘁𝘂𝗺𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘀
Goncalves et al. - The soluble HLA repertoire captures neoantigenic, cryptic, and tumour-associated peptides in melanoma. Molecular & Cellular Proteomics, 2026;101684.
Online: 20 Oct 2026.

In five matched melanoma cases, plasma soluble HLA recovered tumour-associated peptides and a candidate patient-specific neoepitope also found in tumour tissue. This proof of concept does not establish diagnostic sensitivity or specificity.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mcpro.2026.101684

evidence.finding: In five matched melanoma cases, plasma soluble HLA recovered tumour-associated peptides and a candidate patient-specific neoepitope also found in tumour tissue.
evidence.limitation: This proof of concept does not establish diagnostic sensitivity or specificity.
evidence.selectionReason: Matched tissue and plasma address whether circulating HLA can reflect tumour antigen presentation.

sources.label: Publisher abstract, highlights and online date; full text inaccessible.

From our Journal HLA Immune Response Genetics:
• 𝗦𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗶𝘀𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 & 𝗱𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗿 𝗽𝗼𝗽𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀
Saleh et al. - Development and Comparative Evaluation of a Saudi cPRA Calculator for Transplant Sensitisation Assessment. HLA, 2026;108:e70992.
Online: 13 Oct 2026.

A calculator based on 675 Saudi living donors was compared with three international systems across 250 antibody profiles. Despite strong rank correlations, individual estimates differed by up to 48 percentage points. The comparison did not validate estimates against transplant outcomes.

https://doi.org/10.1111/tan.70992

evidence.finding: A calculator based on 675 Saudi living donors was compared with three international systems across 250 antibody profiles. Despite strong rank correlations, individual estimates differed by up to 48 percentage points.
evidence.limitation: The comparison did not validate estimates against transplant outcomes.
evidence.selectionReason: Individual agreement matters even when population-level calculator rankings agree.

sources.label: Publisher-supplied abstract and comparative-study record; first-online date from previously verified candidate record; Wiley full text inaccessible.

Liu et al. - Genome-wide studies define genetic mechanisms of IgA vasculitis. Nature Communications, 2026.
Online: 15 Oct 2026.

In 2,170 cases and 5,928 controls, HLA fine-mapping prioritized DRβ1 position 11 alongside FCAR and INPP5D signals. HLA was imputed; linkage disequilibrium limits causal attribution.

https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-78026-6

evidence.finding: In 2,170 cases and 5,928 controls, HLA fine-mapping prioritized DRβ1 position 11 alongside non-HLA FCAR and INPP5D signals.
evidence.limitation: HLA was imputed; linkage disequilibrium limits causal attribution.
evidence.selectionReason: Substantial multi-cohort disease-immunogenetics study connects HLA peptide-binding variation to myeloid pathways, broadening the recent transplant-heavy selection.

items.text:
• 𝐏𝐞𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐝𝐞 𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐬
Balogh et al. - Predicted structure of the self-immunopeptidome across globally common HLA-I alleles. Scientific Data, 2026.
Online: 12 Nov 2026.

392,976 predicted self-peptide/HLA structures provide a reusable reference for three class I alleles. Head-to-head benchmarking used only 17 independent complexes; natural presentation and T-cell recognition remain untested.

https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-026-08626-w

evidence.finding: 392,976 predicted self-peptide/HLA structures cover three class I alleles; MHC-Fine was compared with APE-Gen 2.0 and AlphaFold 3 on 17 independent complexes.
evidence.limitation: Three alleles and predicted strong-binding nonamers only; structural accuracy does not establish natural presentation or T-cell recognition.
evidence.selectionReason: Reproducible structural resource with training-set exclusions and comparative benchmarking; relevant across alloimmunity, cancer and infection without claiming a validated immunogenicity model.

sources.label: Publisher first-online date and accepted peer-reviewed Data Descriptor status
Full journal PDF: Methods, Data Records, Technical Validation, Tables 1-3, Figs. 2-7 and captions, data/code availability
Publisher-deposited first-online date

items.text:
• 𝐌𝐨𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐥𝐚𝐫 𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠
Trezeguet Renatti et al. - HLA-DQ molecular mismatch predicts acute rejection and donor-specific antibody development after pediatric liver transplantation. Frontiers in Immunology, 2026.
Online: 02 Nov 2026.

In 114 pediatric liver recipients, weighted DQ eplet scores discriminated rejection and dnDQ-DSA better than mismatch counts within the derivation cohort. No independent validation or DQA1 typing; scores remain exploratory.

https://doi.org/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1996061

evidence.finding: In 114 pediatric liver recipients, outcome-weighted DQ eplet scores had higher in-cohort discrimination than mismatch counts for biopsy-proven acute rejection and dnDQ-DSA.
evidence.limitation: Single-center derivation without independent validation or DQA1 typing; missing donor DNA and selective serum testing introduce selection and ascertainment concerns.
evidence.selectionReason: Clinically relevant test of mismatch composition versus burden with prospective follow-up; selected as hypothesis-generating original evidence, not a clinical implementation recommendation.

sources.label: Full publisher main text: 2.1-2.6 Methods, Results, Figs. 2-4/captions, Tables 2-3, Discussion; supplement-specific methods not independently audited
Publisher-deposited first-online date and author

Campos et al. - MARCo: an interactive tool for HLA antibody reactivity in single antigen bead assays. HLA, 2026;108:e71061.
Online: 05 Nov 2026.

MARCo links 70,955 SAB results with serological and molecular comparisons to explore discordant reactivity. Single-laboratory data and limited recent-lot coverage constrain generalizability; clinical utility is unvalidated.

https://doi.org/10.1111/tan.71061

evidence.finding: MARCo integrates 70,955 SAB results with pairwise correlations, HATS serological mapping and HLA-EMMA molecular comparisons across two manufacturers.
evidence.limitation: Single-laboratory retrospective dataset selecting the most positive serum per patient/class/manufacturer; recent lots underrepresented and no external clinical validation.
evidence.selectionReason: Substantial EFI house-journal contribution directly useful for research on SAB interpretation, with explicit limitations of correlation-based inference and platform harmonisation.

• 𝐇𝐒𝐂𝐓 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐢𝐦𝐦𝐮𝐧𝐞 𝐞𝐬𝐜𝐚𝐩𝐞
Tamaki et al. - Adverse impact of deletion of the chromosome 6 on clinical outcomes after allogeneic hematopoietic transplantation. Blood Advances, 2026.
Online: 23 Oct 2026.

Diagnostic del6p was associated with relapse after allogeneic HCT (adjusted HR 1.30). Coexisting cytogenetic abnormalities complicate attribution; reduced HLA-dependent graft-versus-leukemia remains a hypothesis.

https://doi.org/10.1182/bloodadvances.2026021320

evidence.finding: A Japanese registry analysis associated diagnostic del6p with relapse after allogeneic HCT (adjusted HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.02-1.65).
evidence.limitation: Other chromosomal abnormalities confound interpretation; attenuation of HLA-dependent graft-versus-leukemia is a hypothesis, not demonstrated mechanism. Full methods unavailable.
evidence.selectionReason: Original national-registry evidence on pre-transplant immune escape, adds underrepresented HSCT domain; limited to reported association.

sources.label: PubMed full abstract and electronic publication date; no full methods audit

items.text:
• 𝐂𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐫 𝐢𝐦𝐦𝐮𝐧𝐨𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐬
Jackson et al. - Cancer-specific T cell receptor discovery using 150,000 clinical genomics samples. Science Translational Medicine, 2026;18:eaeh8192.
Online: 04 Nov 2026.

Mining approximately 150,000 tumor samples yielded public TCR candidates; 44 TCRs recognized nine peptide-HLA targets in validation assays. These selected-target results do not establish clinical efficacy or comprehensive cross-reactivity safety.

https://doi.org/10.1126/scitranslmed.aeh8192

evidence.finding: Bulk RNA-seq from approximately 150,000 tumors yielded recurrent TCR candidates; 44 paired TCRs were validated for recognition of nine peptide-HLA targets.
evidence.limitation: Selected targets and in-vitro validation do not establish clinical efficacy or comprehensive cross-reactivity safety. Full pairing, discovery/validation independence and safety methods unavailable.
evidence.selectionReason: Large-scale discovery with reported functional TCR validation; brings cancer immunogenetics into the main selection. No therapy recommendation.

sources.label: PubMed full abstract, authors, journal reference and electronic publication date; no full methods audit
Publisher-deposited full journal article and Version-of-Record PDF record

items.text:
From our Journal HLA Immune Response Genetics:
• 𝐇𝐋𝐀 𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐦𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐢𝐧𝐠
Nevarez-Mejia et al. - COMBO-RATE: an experimentally validated bioinformatic tool to identify promiscuous HLA restrictions. HLA, 2026;108:e71060.
Online: 31 Oct 2026.

COMBO-RATE inferred restrictions for 35/43 pertussis epitopes versus 24/43 with RATE; selected new restrictions were confirmed with single-HLA cell lines. Small validation samples and no default multiple-testing correction limit interpretation.

https://doi.org/10.1111/tan.71060

evidence.finding: In a pertussis dataset, COMBO-RATE inferred restrictions for 35/43 dominant CD4 epitopes versus 24/43 with RATE; selected additional restrictions were tested using single-HLA cell lines.
evidence.limitation: Validation uses few donors/selected epitopes; no default multiple-testing correction, and DPA1 is inferred rather than typed. Prioritization output is not universal experimental validation.
evidence.selectionReason: EFI house-journal method extends single-allele inference to promiscuous restrictions and includes functional validation; code and web implementation available.

sources.label: Complete published journal text: Results 2.1-2.6, Figures 1-5/captions, Discussion limitations, Methods 4.1-4.5; supplement not audited
Publisher-deposited 31 October first online date, original journal article status

• 𝗙𝘂𝗻𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗛𝗟𝗔 𝗱𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗶𝘁𝘆
Crivello et al. Peptide-binding motifs define the functional architecture of human leukocyte antigens. Genome Medicine, 2026;18:178.
Online: 12 Nov 2026.

Immunopeptidomics-based clustering identified 40 peptide-binding motif groups across HLA class I and II. Allotypes within groups shared more peptides; class II diversity also reflected alpha-chain pairing and DRB3/4/5. This provides a framework for interpreting HLA variation, but uneven allotype coverage and manually finalized group boundaries limit generalization. Clinical outcomes were not tested in this study.
https://doi.org/10.1186/s13073-026-01825-5

evidence.finding: Motif groups separate peptide repertoires across class I and class II.
evidence.limitation: Uneven experimental coverage; manual group boundaries; clinical benefit untested. Supplementary Table S1, figure captions S1-S16 and Table S2 checked; no independent computational reproduction.
evidence.selectionReason: Pan-HLA antigen presentation with cross-domain relevance. Author Pietro Crivello is an SC member, independent reviewer assessment is required.

sources.label: Publisher full article: Methods, Results, figure captions, Discussion and limitations; supplement not separately audited
Published full text and supplementary PDF; 93 class II heterodimer entries in supplementary Table S2

items.text:
• 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝗶𝗻𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗰𝗲𝗹𝗹 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗽𝘆
Mashhouri et al. Chimeric antigen receptor-engineered ILC2s for targeted immune regulation. Nature Immunology, 2026.
Online: 23 Nov 2026.

Human HLA-A2-targeted CAR-ILC2s reduced T-cell engraftment and improved survival in a xenogeneic GVHD mouse model. CD28/CD3z signalling also induced cytotoxic activity. Small preclinical groups and short persistence leave human safety and efficacy unresolved.
https://doi.org/10.1038/s41590-026-02705-1

evidence.finding: Human HLA-A2-targeted CAR-ILC2s reduced T-cell engraftment and improved survival in a xenogeneic GVHD mouse model. CD28/CD3z signalling also induced cytotoxic activity. Small preclinical groups and short persistence leave human safety and efficacy unresolved.
evidence.limitation: Preclinical mouse model, no human therapeutic outcomes; small groups and limited persistence.
evidence.selectionReason: Mechanistic HLA-directed regulatory cell engineering; links transplantation, innate immunity and synthetic receptors.

sources.label: Publisher PDF: Results, Fig. 4, Methods and statistics; supplementary Fig. 5 independent cohorts and Fig. 6 trafficking examined.

items.text:
• 𝗡𝗞 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗲𝗽𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀, 𝗲𝘃𝗼𝗹𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻
Lavergne et al. Evolution of Natural Killer Cell Receptor Families in Menstruating and Non-menstruating Mammals. Genome Biology and Evolution, 2026;18:evag267.
Online: 22 Oct 2026.

Analysis of 41 mammalian genomes identified previously unannotated KIR/KLR genes. Menstruation was associated with stronger KIR sequence constraint, but not a general receptor-family expansion. Reference-genome sampling and incomplete phenotyping limit inference; uterine function was not tested.
https://doi.org/10.1093/gbe/evag267

evidence.finding: Analysis of 41 mammalian genomes identified previously unannotated KIR/KLR genes. Menstruation was associated with stronger KIR sequence constraint, but not a general receptor-family expansion. Reference-genome sampling and incomplete phenotyping limit inference; uterine function was not tested.
evidence.limitation: One reference genome per species; incomplete phenotype and expression evidence; associations do not establish uterine receptor function.
evidence.selectionReason: Substantial comparative curation with phylogeny-aware analyses; adds underrepresented evolution and reproductive immunogenetics, with eligibility expiring 3 December.

sources.label: Complete PMC journal text, methods, figure captions; supplementary species tables and lineage notes examined.

items.text:
From our Journal HLA Immune Response Genetics:
• 𝗛𝗟𝗔 𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁
Janin et al. Predicting the 1:10 Diluted MFI of Luminex Single Antigen Beads. HLA, 2026;108:e71098.
Online: 23 Nov 2026.

A model fitted to 237,547 paired bead measurements predicted diluted MFI, with 93.9% prediction-interval coverage in primary external validation across four laboratories. Uncertainty widened near saturation. One assay manufacturer was studied; improved patient outcomes were not tested.
https://doi.org/10.1111/tan.71098

evidence.finding: A model fitted to 237,547 paired bead measurements predicted diluted MFI, with 93.9% prediction-interval coverage in primary external validation across four laboratories. Uncertainty widened near saturation. One assay manufacturer was studied; improved patient outcomes were not tested.
evidence.limitation: Retrospective and manufacturer-specific; repeated beads are not independent patients; no transplant outcome validation.
evidence.selectionReason: Substantive house-journal diagnostic modelling with unchanged-model external validation and explicit uncertainty.

sources.label: Full Methods, Results, Discussion and supplementary methods/tables S1-S3 read; supplementary figure captions S1-S10 checked.
